newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli planes hit in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes hit in south Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli aircraft launched on Thursday the fourth attack in less than a week against suspected Hizbollah bases in Lebanon, security souces said.

They said two warplanes fired two air-to-surface rockets into the Jabal Safi and Mleita areas in the Iqlim al-Toufah ridge, a bastion for the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the latest air raid.
Earlier, Hizbollah guerrillas fired mortar bombs into the Israeli outpost of Braachit on the edge of the occupation zone causing no casualties, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

Thursday's air raid was the fourth Israeli air attack against Hizbollah targets in less than a week. On Wednesday, Israeli planes struck twice -- in the early morning and shortly after nightfall -- into the Iqlim.
On Sunday, Israeli aircraft targeted other suspected Hizbollah targets in southeast Lebanon after a clash between Israeli troops and the Moslem guerrillas.
No one was injured in any of the three air attacks.

Last Tuesday, a five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon said at least one Katyusha rocket was fired from south Lebanon into Israel on Friday night. The monitors however did not reprimand Lebanon.
The Katyusha was the first fired at northern Israel since an April 26 understanding which ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in which 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed.
Hizbollah, which fired volleys of Katyushas at Israel before the ceasefire, has denied responsibility for the firing of the rockets.
